findings.issue: contradicts task clause: 'Apply it to every case in this suite that hands one mark file to commands that run at the same time' / acceptance (1) 'no case hands one file to two commands that run at the same time'. au32 runs a real `auto` drive over _auto_writer_wave_repo (a wave of width 2); auto_run starts a wave's members together (drive-phase.py auto_run, Popen per command), and both writer-stub sessions append one json line each to the one WS_LOG file (_WRITER_STUB opens it with 'a'), and the case asserts len(_stub_runs(log)) == 2. That is the same shared-append shape the task fixes for au31. The executor's class sweep says WS_LOG is 'written by sessions run one at a time', which is false for au32. Mitigation I verified: au32 is skipped where os.killpg is absent (Windows), and O_APPEND is atomic on POSIX, so it cannot lose a line on the platform that went red; the defect is the unmet clause and the inaccurate claim, not a known red.
findings.resolution: Either give each wave member's stub a log of its own (e.g. a per-session WS_LOG derived from WS_SESSION/pid, read together through a directory-reading helper like _auto_marks), or leave au32 as is and state in _auto_marks's docstring and the outcome why it is exempt (POSIX-only, atomic O_APPEND) and correct the class-sweep claim.

intent.note: Matched clauses: the helper _auto_marks (tests/test_drive_phase.py:11822) now takes a file, a list or a directory and returns the same list of lines, with a docstring naming which cases need which; _auto_wave_member (:12198) gives each wave member its own <subject>.log; au30, au30b and au31 read the directory; au36/au37 and _auto_cases keep one serial file and their order; au31 still asserts the same values by value and au31c asserts two distinct files read off the wave step's own runs (argv[3] of _auto_command, which is [exe,-c,child,mark,code]); only the test file changes. The honest 'could not show it on POSIX' reproduction is stated. Diverges on one clause: 'every case in this suite that hands one mark file to commands that run at the same time' - au32 (:12378-12388) starts two writer-stub sessions together as a wave, both appending to one WS_LOG, and was not changed. The executor's claim that WS_LOG writers 'run one at a time' does not describe au32. The staged table is unchanged and the helpers are module-level, so the second named dependant holds. Case count: au31c is added, none removed.
